about_the_game:
This is a demo version featuring a girl from Gunma Prefecture. You can play up to Stage 3!

The full version includes all 8 stages plus secret elements, but this demo lets you enjoy the first 3 stages.

All other gameplay elements are the same as the full version.

We hope you enjoy it—it was made just for you!

This is a pseudo-retro 2D side-scrolling shooting game. Inspired by the MSX standard popular in 1980s Japan, it features enhanced visuals (TMS9918A with V9938 palette) and sound (PSG+SCC), offering diverse gameplay across 8 stages.

Originally released for smartphones in 2014 and later passing Steam Greenlight, the release was delayed by about a decade due to the developer's busy schedule (Final Re:Quest The Movie). As a result, the game has been significantly expanded.

The controls are simple and familiar. You control an adorable pixel-art girl, shooting automatically to defeat various enemies.

Drawing inspiration from classic Japanese culture and Gunma’s nature and traditions, this 80s-style game lets you discover hidden items in stages that may change the ending. It aims to capture the simple, kitschy charm of shooters before the bullet-hell era. With unique content you won’t find elsewhere, it’s perfect for those tired of complex modern games.

For those wanting more details, here’s something extra! You get 5 lives, a barrier that can withstand two hits, and 5 continues!

The game has 8 stages (3 in the demo), but the full version includes 3 hidden stages. It may seem simple, but the conditions to unlock the third hidden stage are tough—most players won’t manage it.

Your only attack is the shot—no weak stuff like bombers here. There’s also no saving or achievements. Tired of chasing bloated achievement lists? Don’t worry—this game doesn’t have them to begin with.
